Bill.BriefDescription: Regarding the use of the life sciences discovery fund for human stem cell research.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the use of the life sciences discovery fund forhuman stem cell research; adding a new section to chapter 68.50 RCW;adding a new section to chapter 43.350 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature supports the use of stemcell research including projects funded through the life sciencesdiscovery fund to treat and prevent serious and debilitating diseasesand conditions, including Parkinson's disease, diabetes, strokes, andbirth defects. The legislature recognizes careful nationaldeliberations in law, ethics, and sciences through the nationalacademies of science and the legislature intends to promote biomedicalresearch for the benefit of all patients, including stem cell researchin Washington state consistent with national recommendations andprocesses.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 68.50 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Except as specified in subsection (2) of this section, humanstem cells from any source may be donated for research purposes if the p. 1 SHB 1730donor has provided written consent to use the human stem cells for suchpurposes and the donor has not received valuable consideration for thedonation. (2)(a) Individuals may donate human embryonic stem cells forresearch purposes if the human embryonic stem cells are obtained fromblastocysts that are generated by in vitro fertilization procedures,the donation is made pursuant to the valid informed consent of both thedonors of the sperm and egg that created the blastocyst, and the donorhas not received valuable consideration for the donation. (b) Informed consent to donate human embryonic stem cells forresearch is valid only if both the sperm and egg donors acknowledge inwriting that they have been informed of the opportunity for disposingof blastocysts through: Donating the blastocyst for research purposes;donating the blastocyst to another person; thawing the blastocystwithout further action; or disposing of the blastocyst in anothermethod. (c) In the event that a sperm or egg donor has died or has provideda written relinquishment of his or her right to select the dispositionof the blastocyst to the other donor, the other donor may select thedisposition of the blastocyst. (3) For purposes of this section: (a) "Blastocyst" means a preimplantation embryo consisting ofapproximately one hundred fifty cells that are organized into an innerand outer cell layer surrounding a fluidfilled cavity. The cells ofthe inner layer, from which embryonic stem cells are derived, consistsof undifferentiated cells that have the potential to become any type ofcell in the human body. (b) "Valuable consideration" has the same meaning as in RCW68.50.610.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.350 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) No money from the life sciences discovery fund may be used tosupport research involving human stem cells, including human embryonicstem cells, unless the human stem cells were donated in compliance withsection 2 of this act. (2) No public funds may be distributed for the following purposes: SHB 1730 p. 2 (a) No money from the life sciences discovery fund may be used toinjure an embryo that has been implanted in a uterus. (b) No money from the life sciences discovery fund may be used toclone an individual by means of asexual reproduction of a human beingby transplanting a blastocyst that has been created by somatic cellnuclear transfer into a uterus or substitute for a uterus with thepurpose of creating a human being.
